_README: Code-table knob for the tbl_use_case integer columns. Editing this file changes what the
assistant says; no code change is needed. Same seam as config/rule_text_semantics.json.
WHY PROVENANCE IS A FIELD HERE, not a comment:
business_category has THREE sources and they do not agree, so 'is this code legal' has three
different answers depending on who you ask:
1. the DATA DICTIONARY (owner-relayed screenshot, 2026-08-05) defines 0-7 and stops there;
2. BusinessCategoryEnum.java on the mirror additionally defines 8, 10-21, 32, 34, 35;
3. the real UAT rows additionally CONTAIN 33 (1 row, B0001) and 37 (6 rows, I0135-I0140),
all with status=Y, i.e. active.
Flattening those into one 'known enum' is what produced the earlier claim that 33/37 were
'unregistered new categories'. They are not: nothing defines them anywhere. Codes 8-35, by
contrast, ARE defined — just not in the dictionary excerpt we were shown, which is a weaker
statement and must not be reported as drift.
So each entry carries the source that defines it, and only a code defined by NEITHER source is
a data-contract defect. A code in `code_enum` but not `data_dictionary` is reported as such and
is NOT an alarm — the dictionary excerpt may simply be older or narrower than the code.
The table these columns belong to is inferred from the neighbouring columns in the same
screenshot (bounce_back periods, mi_category, has_order_status, send_mode) which match
tbl_use_case. If that inference is ever contradicted, fix it here rather than in code.
Adding a code: put it under the source that actually defines it. Never move a code into
`data_dictionary` to silence a warning.

business_category._source: data dictionary screenshot relayed by the project owner, 2026-08-05

code_enum._source: BusinessCategoryEnum.java on the mirror — defined in code, absent from the dictionary excerpt above

_note: An INDEPENDENT third statement of the send semantics that tbl_use_case_ext.rule_text and
tbl_use_case_channel_rule.priority both also describe. The three map onto each other:
send_mode 3 (single channel)<-> rule_text no operator, or '|' (exclusive_choice)
That mapping is used ONLY to CROSS-CHECK rule_text, never to override it: rule_text stays
authoritative per the 2026-07-27 owner answer. A disagreement is reported as a data-quality
finding, exactly like the existing rule_text-vs-priority disagreement.
This column is bound optimistically — absent from the export just means the cross-check does
not run, and nothing else changes.
